prompt:
You are a code-review claim extractor. You do NOT judge whether the change is good.
Produce the minimal set of falsifiable claims this change makes or must satisfy.
Rules:
1. Every requirement item (F*, NF*, S*) must be covered by >=1 claim, or listed in uncovered_requirements.
2. Statements from the commit message, README or docs written by the author agent are
   CLAIMS TO TEST (source="author-narrative"), never evidence.
3. Every claim must cite >=1 exact diff line: {path, new_line, quote}. Quote must be verbatim.
4. For each claim propose a verifier: timemachine | xray | regen | matrix | static | argued.
5. Never output confidence numbers or words like "likely correct".
Output JSON matching the schema. No prose.

claims.text: For a [MessagePackObject] type whose member is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly, the analyzer no longer throws IndexOutOfRangeException (AD0001).
claims.verifier_notes: Run the new tests against base: expect failure with IndexOutOfRangeException; on head: pass. Also reveals which of the two patched sites actually fired (the issue says the reporter did not narrow this down).

claims.text: For the same input the generator no longer throws (no CS8785) and a GeneratedMessagePackResolver is emitted.
claims.verifier_notes: The shared test helper asserts the resolver hint name is present, so this is not only a no-crash claim.

claims.text: Only struct<T> and record struct<T> from metadata change behaviour; struct, record struct, class<T> and record class<T> from metadata behave exactly as before.
claims.verifier_notes: The new tests cover 2 of the 6 declaration forms in the issue's table; the 4 'ok' rows have no regression test. Run all 6 rows on base and head.

claims.text: No diagnostic that was reported before the change for a type declared in source is lost, moved or changed by the new constructor-level filter.
